We aggregate all bug reports in a spatial database and prioritize them by cluster size. So if you report a bug that isn't in a major cluster or itself affecting a lot of people - we'd handle it later.. There are over 100,000 reports we sorted this way 🙃 On top of that we also manually review bugs but due to the size of the dataset we can't manually review every bug. So individual tracking wouldn't really represent how we look at it because it may be looked at as part of a cluster but individually it's just a datapoint in a bigger galaxy of bugs.

My take on this: SBMM is often poorly done in multiplayer team games. For players it often feels like they are thrown into  team that matches another team, while the individual performance and playstyle is secondary. 
Generally X% of matches are lost no matter what you do. Y% of matches are won no matter what you do. And finally Z% of matches actually depend on your performance.
SBMM in team games with randoms feels like the X and Y are way too large. The expectation should be that you always have to try and this is actually the case when you reach the very top of the ladder. 
The issue is really in the middle where you also have strong differences in teammate performance - I have seen players and streamers go full tilt and enter a massive decay streak losing match after match because they play well below their performance. 
The other thing is that in top play you generally have people who mastered the game and they can swap roles  or tactics to play the other team. The middle ranks often have people stuck with one-tricks and single tactics which gives them a certain win-rate but it keeps them there, so that it's very easy to get frustrated when this player rather loses than play what is needed.
Generally SBMM is supposed to fix something but just shifts the problem and you end up with players rather wanting none again and occasionally run into the pro with no real-life to get absolutely railed but at least not lose rank points or ELO for losing.
